newsitem.title: USA: Army sex case a "tragedy," fresh probe underway.
newsitem.headline: Army sex case a "tragedy," fresh probe underway.

text.p: The top U.S. military officer said Monday the unfolding rape and sexual harassment scandal at Aberdeen Proving Ground in Maryland was a tragedy and vowed to prosecute those found guilty.
"It's a great, great tragedy," Gen. John Shalikashvili, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, said on ABC Television's "Good Morning America."
Meanwhile, a fresh investigation on sexual misconduct by several supervisers was launched at Fort Leonard Wood Army base in southeast Missouri.

"Our task now is to ensure that we find out exactly just how widespread it is and bring to justice all those who should be brought to justice," Shalikashvili said of the scandal. "But it is also important to put it in perspective," he added, saying 1.5 million Americans in the military should not "be painted with the same brush."

About 20 people have been suspended from their duties at the training base north of Baltimore pending an investigation into allegations of sexual harassment, and Army Capt. Craig Minnick said Saturday, "We do expect some additional charges to be ... filed."

The Army has moved quickly to deal with the scandal. Three male trainers, including two drill instructors, were charged Thursday in connection with alleged coerced sex and sexual harassment. The allegations involve at least 17 women at the Army Ordnance and Doctrine Command's training facility, where newly enlisted young men and women are taught Army skills.
The three men charged, including a captain who was a company commander, helped train hundreds of young recruits in tasks from handling ammunition to repairing trucks.

At Fort Leonard Wood, Maj. Steve Rego, an Army spokesman, confirmed that criminal investigators were pursuing separate allegations ranging from fraternisation to rape against several supervisors. The probe was reported in the Washington Post Monday.
